actions.body: When autonomous systems learn preferences from interactions or feedback, the sequence of updates matters profoundly. Recent findings demonstrate that inferential errors and belief updates under model misspecification are generally path-dependent, meaning that the trajectory of experience directly influences the final preference profile rather than converging to a unique universal state. By integrating general preference oracle frameworks that do not rely on rigid reward function assumptions, we gain a clearer view of how agents adapt. Summary: Preference learning is sensitive to the path of past experiences, showing that an agent's history shapes its goals in lasting ways.
actions.lede: Exploring how models develop preferences over time and why path dependence shapes autonomous agent stability.
